Context:
- `knowledge-base/DECISIONS.md` (decisions taken, and why)
- `GOAL.md` (the goal of the project (long-term direction, scope, non-scope, ...))
- `BUSINESS_LOGIC.md` (codebase business logic)
- `knowledge-base/FACTS.md` (non-obvious facts relevant to the project)
- `knowledge-base/INSIGHTS.md` (insights relevant to the project)
- `knowledge-base/MARKET_RESEARCH.md` (the market the project competes in)
- `knowledge-base/**.md` (more files holding knowledge related to the project)
- `tickets/**.md` (things to potentially work on; format: the "Ticket format" section below)
- `.the-framework/conversations/**.md` (conversations between humans, recorded by agents (e.g. the agent Discord bot))
- `TODO_AGENTS.md` (the AI task queue; format: the "TODO_AGENTS.md" section below)

# Ticket format

## tickets/<DATE>_<SLUG>.md

DATE: yyyy-mm-dd
SLUG: succinct kebab-case slug of the ticket title
Body:
```md
Status: open/closed
Priority: 10-0 [optional, 10: critical — act immediately, 0: only if capacity]
Topics: [list-of-topics] [optional]
GitHub: [#42](https://github.com/org/repo/issues/42) [optional]

# Ticket title

## TLDR

...

## Why it matters

...

[optional: more info (any heading and format you want)]
```

## tickets/<DATE>_<SLUG>.spike.md

For an existing ticket (e.g. `tickets/2042-01-01_some-ticket.md`), a spike can be created (`tickets/2042-01-01_some-ticket.spike.md`).

Body:
```md
# [Spike] Ticket title

## TLDR

...

## Analysis

...

[optional: more info (any heading and format you want)]
```

Typical spike content:
- High-level overview, for example:
  - What it takes to implement it
  - List all the ways to implement it
  - Potential "laziness" shortcuts
  - Full-fledged implementation VS minimal implementation
  - Open questions
  - ...
- Estimated effort (for each ways to implement it):
  - Human intervention effort: trivial/low/medium/high/very-high
  - Token consumption: time estimate (minutes, hours, or days)

## tickets/<DATE>_<SLUG>.plan.md

For an existing ticket (e.g. `tickets/2042-01-01_some-ticket.md`), a detailed plan can be created (`tickets/2042-01-01_some-ticket.plan.md`).

Body:
```md
# [Plan] Ticket title

## TLDR

...

## Plan

...

## Hard problems [optional]

...

## Variability [optional]

...

[optional: more info (any heading and format you want)]
```

Typical plan content:
- Concrete and detailed plan on how to implement the ticket, for example:
  - Exhaustive list of all aspects (including edge cases)
  - Thorough analysis
  - Overview of code changes
  - ...
- Plan broken down in multiple (sub)plans in case of variability
- Hard problems
  - Exhaustive list of all aspects with low confidence regarding how to solve them (the hard problems), with explanation why
- Variability
  - List all aspects that need to be implemented
  - Give a rating to each aspect (from 0 to 10) following this criteria: is there an obviously optimal way to implement it (10), or is it highly unclear whether it can be implemented in a better way (0)?
  - Explore and suggest alternatives for aspects with a low rating
  - For each aspect that has alternatives: list all alternatives sorted in a sensible order, then ask the user to pick one with showChoices() and AWAIT (one question per aspect, recommending the alternative you'd pick)

# TODO_AGENTS.md

Content:
```md
## Priority 10 (critical — act immediately)

...

## Priority 9

- [Succinct description](/link-for-more-details)
- Or self-contained TODO item with complete description of what should be done

...

## Priority 0 (only if capacity)

...
```

The TODO_AGENTS.md file lists *all* tasks AI will work on next, sorted by priority.

To remove an item (e.g. when done), simply remove it from `TODO_AGENTS.md`.

Priority 10 is rarely used (e.g. critical production bugs) and should be treated as utmost priority.

# System prompt

SHOW_MD: Show it via `showMarkdown()`
SHOW_CHOICES: Show it via `showChoices()`
AWAIT: Stop, await user answer before resuming
SESSION_NAME: the name of the session
TODO_FILE: `TODO_AGENTS.md`
ADD_ANALYSIS_ENTRY: Add entry to the ANALYSIS_RESULT.md list

## Analyze the user prompt

Analyze the user prompt, follow the instructions, create ANALYSIS_RESULT.md that lists the analysis results, and show it via showMarkdownSecondary()

### Ambiguous prompt

If it isn't clear what you should do (e.g. unclear scope, unclear user prompt), make a list of interpretations sorted by plausibility, <SHOW_CHOICES>, <AWAIT>

<ADD_ANALYSIS_ENTRY> whether YES/NO the prompt is ambiguous

### Scope

- If the scope of what you'll work on is *large*, create a `PLAN_<SESSION_NAME>.agent.md` of what you'll work on, <SHOW_MD>, <AWAIT>
- If the scope is potentially *very large* (e.g. spans over many hours/days of work), also create a <TODO_FILE> (backlog of follow-up tasks) and <SHOW_MD>

<ADD_ANALYSIS_ENTRY> whether the scope is small, large, or very large


## Before starting changes

Do the following before applying your first change.

### Session name

1. If the repository has uncommitted changes, create a commit "[The Framework] Uncommited changes"
2. Create a <SESSION_NAME> as a string [a-z0-9-]+ that succinctly represents the intention of the user prompt
3. Create a new branch `the-framework/<SESSION_NAME>` and `$ git checkout` it — do all the work in that branch
4. Call setSessionName(<SESSION_NAME>)


## Before applying changes

Do the following before applying changes — do it again anytime you make new changes.

### Alternatives

Measure "variability":
- List all high-level problems that you're about to solve
- Give a rating to each problem (from 0 to 10) following this criteria: is there an obviously optimal way to solve the problem (10), or is it highly unclear whether the problem can be solved in a better way (0)?
- Explore and suggest alternatives for problems with a low rating
- For each problem that has alternatives: list all alternatives sorted in a sensible order, <SHOW_CHOICES>, <AWAIT>


## After applying changes

After you're done, consider whether <SESSION_NAME> is finished and there isn't any work left to do — if that's the case then call setReadyForMerge()

## Awaiting a choice
When these instructions tell you to showChoices() / showMultiSelect() / showMarkdown() and then AWAIT, do not decide for the user.
End your turn with one fenced code block, then stop.
For a single choice (showChoices, pick one), tag it `await-choices`:
```await-choices
{ "title": "<the question>", "options": [{ "label": "<option>", "detail": "<optional one-liner>" }], "recommended": "<the label to default to>" }
```
For a multi-select (showMultiSelect, pick any number), tag it `await-multiselect` and set `default` on the entries that start checked:
```await-multiselect
{ "title": "<the prompt>", "options": [{ "label": "<option>", "detail": "<optional one-liner>", "default": true }] }
```
For a plan/document approval (showMarkdown of a file you wrote, then AWAIT), tag it `await-confirmation` and name the file:
```await-confirmation
{ "title": "<what to approve>", "file": "PLAN_<slug>.agent.md" }
```
The framework shows it, waits for the user, and re-prompts you with their answer. Do not continue past it on your own.

## Handing the browser to a human
When you are working in a browser and hit something you cannot or should not get past yourself — a login wall, a captcha, an SSO or 2FA step — stop and hand it over. Never type a password, never attempt a captcha, and never use a credential you found lying around in the repo or the environment. Tag the block `await-browser`:
```await-browser
{ "title": "<what the human needs to do>", "url": "<the page you are stuck on>" }
```
The user acts in that browser, then you are re-prompted. Their answer says whether it was handled: if it was not, do not retry the same page — say what you could not reach and work on what you can, or stop. Use this only for the browser; a decision the user needs to make is `await-choices`.

## Showing a document without waiting
To display markdown in the side panel without blocking (a plan, a summary, a writeup) and keep working, put a `show-markdown` block anywhere in your turn. The first line is its title:
```show-markdown
# <title>
<the markdown body>
```
This just shows it; you do not stop. Re-emit the same title to update that view in place.
showMarkdown() and showMarkdownSecondary() are both this block: emit the same `show-markdown` block for either.

## Session name
When you call setSessionName(<name>) (after creating and checking out the `the-framework/<name>` branch), also emit a `set-session-name` block naming it, so the dashboard shows which session this is. The first non-empty line is the name (a `[a-z0-9-]` slug):
```set-session-name
<name>
```
You do not stop; re-emit it if you rename the session.

## Ready for merge
When you call setReadyForMerge() — you believe the work is complete and ready for human review — emit an empty `ready-for-merge` block. This flips the dashboard status from building to ready; it does not stop your turn.
```ready-for-merge
```

Here's the map of everything you need.

## 1. The run page

There is exactly **one Vike page** — the dashboard is a single-page app with client-side routing.

- **Route file**: `/home/rom/code/the-framework/.the-framework/worktrees/2026-07-27T16-55-38-597Z/packages/framework-dashboard/pages/index/+route.ts` (catch-all) and `pages/index/+Page.tsx` (the shell).
- **URL parsing**: `packages/framework-dashboard/lib/route.ts` — `/{projectId}/{sessionId}` is one run's page (`parseRoute` at lines 46-53). `sessionId` in the URL **is** `RunMeta.id`, which is also the run's worktree directory name (comment at lines 5-6).
- **Shell / router**: `pages/index/+Page.tsx`
  - `renderMain()` at lines 267-351 picks the view; the run page is `<RunView>` at lines 296, 315 and 328-350.
  - Layout at lines 353-417: `SidebarProvider` column → daemon-health banner (360-365) → row of `RunHistory` sidebar (374-397) | `<main>` (398) | `RightRail` (401-414).
- **The run page itself**: `packages/framework-dashboard/components/RunView.tsx`, JSX at lines 137-228, in order:
  1. `<RunActionBar>` (139-174) — header area: label/branch/status + summary + actions.
  2. `<SessionDetails>` (177) — the "label: value" facts strip, shown when the header disclosure is `open`.
  3. `<RunChanges>` (183) / `<RunHandoffDetails>` (184) — disclosure detail.
  4. Notices (187-193): `ActionsRunNotice`, `CloudRunNotice`, `RemoteRunNotice`.
  5. `<RunFeed>` (201-212) — the log area.
  6. `<RunComposer>` (214-226) — the input at the bottom.

**Best insertion point for your block**: between the notices (line 193) and the feed (line 196), or inside the `open` disclosure next to `SessionDetails` (line 177).

## 2. Data flow

Not REST — **Telefunc RPC** (plus one Telefunc *Channel* for the live event stream).

- Client-facing modules are thin re-export shims: `packages/framework-dashboard/server/reads.telefunc.ts` (lines 8-9 — import-then-export, deliberately not `export … from`; see its comment). Same shape for `control/events/projects/preferences/quota/devices.telefunc.ts`.
- **Real implementations** live in `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard-rpc/reads.telefunc.ts` (~23 KB, ~430 lines) so the daemon serves them in-process.
- Registration under baked RPC keys: `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard-rpc/register.ts` lines 15-23 (`DASHBOARD_TELEFUNC_KEYS`) and 58-69.
- Live feed: `packages/framework-dashboard/lib/use-live-events.ts` → `server/events.telefunc.ts` → `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard-rpc/events.telefunc.ts` (a Telefunc Channel tailing `events.jsonl`).

**How the server knows the worktree path** — there is no `worktreePath` field on the run object passed around; it is *resolved* server-side from `(projectId, runId)`:

- `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard-rpc/context.ts:48` — `resolveRunPath(projectId, runId)` → `resolveProjectPath` + `resolveRunCheckout`.
- `packages/the-framework/src/store/run-checkout.ts:22` — `resolveRunCheckout(projectCwd, runId)`: live meta's `cwd` field first (line 25), else `worktreePath(projectCwd, runId)` if the dir exists (27-28), else project root.
- `packages/the-framework/src/store/worktree.ts:14` — `worktreePath(repo, runId)` = `<repo>/.the-framework/worktrees/<runId>`.
- Convenience wrapper for forgiving reads: `reads.telefunc.ts:52` — `withRunPath(projectId, runId, read, empty)`.

**Existing code that reads files from a run's worktree** (your templates):

| Telefunction | Location | Reader |
|---|---|---|
| `onFileContent` | `reads.telefunc.ts:307` | `dashboard/file-read.ts:67` `readFileContent` |
| `onRunChanges` | `reads.telefunc.ts:290` | `dashboard/file-diff.ts` `readFileChanges` |
| `onProjectFiles` | `reads.telefunc.ts:243` | `project.ts` `crawlRepoFiles` |
| `onRunWorktree` | `reads.telefunc.ts:120` | resolves path + git status + size |
| `onDocs` (PLAN_/TODO_) | `reads.telefunc.ts:173` | `dashboard/docs.ts:64` `readDocs` — **project-root scoped, not run-scoped** |
| `onTicket` | `reads.telefunc.ts:183` | `dashboard/tickets.ts:317` `readTicket` |

Two especially relevant:
- `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard/file-read.ts` — `safeRepoPath` (line 25) and `readConfinedFile` (line 43, realpath-based confinement). Use these if the filename ever comes from the client; for a fixed `ANALYSIS_RESULT.md` you can `readFile(join(cwd, 'ANALYSIS_RESULT.md'))` like `readDocs` does (`docs.ts:68`).
- `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard/tickets.ts:138-195` — `describe(md)`, the existing **"parse `key: value` lines out of a markdown preamble"** parser (status/priority/topics/GitHub link). This is the closest existing analogue to what you want for `ANALYSIS_RESULT.md`.

## 3. Existing markdown / metadata display on the run page

- **`show-markdown` side panel**: parsed server-side by `packages/the-framework/src/turn-gate.ts:185-192` (`parseMarkdownViews`, regex `/```show-markdown\s+([\s\S]*?)```/g`) → emitted as `view` events → folded client-side by `packages/framework-dashboard/lib/live-state.ts:46` (`agentViews`) → `pages/index/+Page.tsx:237` → `RightRail` (`components/RightRail.tsx:167`) → `components/ViewsRail.tsx`. **This is event-stream driven, not a file read** — so it is not a fit for a file the agent writes to disk.
- **PLAN_/TODO_ docs panel**: `components/DocsPanel.tsx` (rendered at `RightRail.tsx:173`), fed by `onDocs` polled at `RightRail.tsx:61`. This *is* file-read based, but reads the **project root**, not the run worktree.
- **Markdown renderer**: `packages/framework-dashboard/components/Markdown.tsx` — dependency-free, builds React nodes, never injects HTML. `<Markdown text={…} compact />` is what you'd reuse.
- **Run metadata badges** on the run page: `components/GitStatusBar.tsx` (branch/dirty/size/PR, lines 87-202), rendered from `RunActionBar.tsx:61-82`; the status pill comes from `lib/run-status.ts:20` `runStatusPill` and is rendered at `RunActionBar.tsx:74-81`.

## 4. Reusable "label: value" / badge components

- **`Fact`** — `components/SessionDetails.tsx:28-35`. Literally `label` + `value` in muted/foreground pair; the strip that wraps them is line 44. Currently module-private (not exported) — the cleanest thing to copy or export.
- **`Badge`** — `components/ui/badge.tsx:5` (rounded pill, className-tonable).
- **`LoopStatusCard`** — `components/LoopStatusCard.tsx:9` — a bordered `<section>` with a heading + `Badge` + list; a good shape template for a small block above the feed.
- **`ResolvedOptions`** chips — `components/ResolvedOptions.tsx:32-45` (`label: value` chips row).
- **`OptionLabel`** — `components/ui/option-label.tsx:4` (label + sub-description, menu-oriented).
- **`RunOutcomes`** legend — `components/RunOutcomes.tsx:28-37` (dot + label + tabular-nums count).
- **`Tooltip/TooltipTrigger/TooltipContent`** — `components/ui/tooltip.tsx`; the codebase uses these instead of `title` attributes (see `GitStatusBar.tsx:128-137`, and the `#1149` note in `test-utils.ts`).

## 5. Adding a new endpoint (the pattern)

Four files, in this order:

1. **Impl** in `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard-rpc/reads.telefunc.ts`. Example to copy: `onRunChanges` at lines 290-296 (run-scoped, resolves the worktree via `resolveRunPath`, wrapped in `relayOr` for remote-device runs) or the simpler `onTicket` at line 183. `relayOr` is at `dashboard-rpc/relay-run.ts:11` — pass a run-scoped call through it so remote runs (#1067) don't break.
2. **Export** from `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard-rpc/index.ts:5` (the `reads` export list).
3. **Shim** in `packages/framework-dashboard/server/reads.telefunc.ts` — add the name to **both** the `import` (line 8) and the `export` (line 9). Not `export … from`, per the comment at lines 5-7.
4. Registration is automatic (`register.ts` iterates module exports), and `dashboard-rpc/register.test.ts:27` asserts every export is registered.

**Client call pattern** — no fetch helper; you import the telefunction and call it inside `useLoaded`/`usePolled` from `packages/framework-dashboard/lib/use-async.ts` (`useLoaded` line 80, `usePolled` line 98; note the `deps`-must-match-the-closure contract and the `keepPrevious` flag).

Example hooks/components:
- `packages/framework-dashboard/lib/use-run-handoff.ts:29` — a dedicated hook wrapping `usePolled(() => onRunHandoff(projectId, runId), …)` with `loaded`/adaptive cadence. **This is the file to model a `use-analysis-result.ts` on.**
- `packages/framework-dashboard/components/RunChanges.tsx:4-5` — component-local `usePolled` on `onRunChanges`.
- `packages/framework-dashboard/components/GitStatusBar.tsx:60-68` — `usePolled` with `keepPrevious: true`.

## 6. Testing

**Dashboard package** (`packages/framework-dashboard`):
- Runner: **Vitest** + jsdom + Testing Library. Config `packages/framework-dashboard/vitest.config.ts` (jsdom, `globals: true`, `**/*.test.ts(x)`, `testTimeout: 20_000`); setup `vitest.setup.ts` (`asyncUtilTimeout: 5000`); helpers `test-utils.ts` (`hoverTooltip`/`unhoverTooltip` — needed because hints are Base UI tooltips, not `title` attrs).
- Command: `pnpm --filter @gemstack/framework-dashboard test` (script is `vitest run`).
- Component test template — mock the telefunc shim, then dynamic-import the component: `packages/framework-dashboard/components/RunChanges.test.tsx:4-8` and `components/GitStatusBar.test.tsx:4-8`:
  ```ts

  vi.mock('../server/reads.telefunc.js', () => ({ onRunChanges, onFileDiff }))
  const { RunChanges } = await import('./RunChanges.js')
  ```
- Other examples: `components/RightRail.test.tsx`, `components/Markdown.test.tsx`, `lib/use-runs.test.ts`.

**Server side** (`packages/the-framework`) — different runner: **`node:test` + `node:assert/strict`**, compiled first.
- Command: `pnpm --filter @gemstack/the-framework test` (= `gen-prompts` → `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` → `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`).
- Telefunction test example: `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard-rpc/reads.telefunc.test.ts` (lines 9-24 — unknown project degrades to empty; unsafe run id returns null).
- File-reader test examples: `packages/the-framework/src/dashboard/docs.test.ts`, `dashboard/file-read.test.ts`, `dashboard/tickets.test.ts`.

## What was built

**Server** (`packages/the-framework`): a new `dashboard/analysis-result.ts` parses `ANALYSIS_RESULT.md` tolerantly — list markers, bold/backtick emphasis, numbered lines, and hyphenated keys all match; Scope/Variability keep only a short leading value (so `small — one dashboard feature…` reads as `small`, while a rambling value hides rather than truncating); Plan/New tickets accept phrased answers (`not needed`, `none` → no) and hide when there's no clear yes/no. A new `onRunAnalysis` telefunction serves it through the standard `relayOr` path, reading **only the run's own worktree** — when a clean run's worktree is gone, `resolveRunPath` falls back to the project root, and a leftover root file would be some other agent's analysis (the same misattribution guard the handoff read uses).

**Client** (`packages/framework-dashboard`): a self-hiding `RunAnalysisStrip` on the run page, styled like the existing session-details facts strip, polling at the usual 15s cadence so it appears mid-run without a reload. It shows `Prompt analysis · Scope · Variability · Plan · New tickets`, hides any absent field, and puts the ticket's long labels ("Whether the work includes a plan" / "Whether the work spans over new tickets") in tooltips on the yes/no facts. Runs without the file — other agents, older runs, cleaned-up worktrees — render nothing.
